Turn 5: 'Verdict: runbook bug, not a tool bug. The non-abort was the correct outcome for the fixture as written' — consistent with _abort_on_a_source_filter_that_denies_its_own_apps reading flatpak's listing.

Diff §4 item 2 'apt, second round … This round exists for the questions only the first round's answers can settle, which is why both come after every screen above'.

Diff §4 item 4 'flatpak. `io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith` left at install', between snap and manual installs.
Turn 10 reply and §4 item 5 explain the scan reads one level down, either answer legitimate, runbook walks one-application branch to leave a single finding for §6.
Diff §4 item 5: '/opt/pcsw-uat-app first, answered y … /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor second, answered x'.
Turn 12: dry run does not hold snapd auto-refresh so pc2 drifted back onto pc1's revision; noted 'since I can't look at your machines' and pointed to the DEBUG log.
Turn 12: `ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'sudo snap refresh --revision=<that second revision> hello && snap list hello'` then run again.
Diff §4: 'Re-pin `hello` on pc2 before EVERY run below, including a repeated dry run' with the refresh line before both the dry run and the real run.
Replay reports `codespell` clean after each edit; only the runbook markdown changed, so ruff/basedpyright/pytest not required.

judge.reason: Every divergence was diagnosed with a verdict, the VM-unreachability was stated and the replay reasoned from ADR-020 and the code, and the runbook diff fixes the filter, §3 prose, collateral key, second-round wording, the two missing install questions, the review order, and the re-pin instruction. Doubt remains only on c1 (cannot see the runbook's later checks to confirm consistency) and on whether codespell was run repo-wide.
